Tidewater: project overview

Tidewater syncs tide-gauge readings from coastal sensors into one queryable store, so the harbor team can plan around the water instead of guessing. It replaces the old nightly cron scripts.

Goals

  • Ingest readings within 60 seconds of capture
  • Keep 10 years of history at 1-minute resolution — about 5 million rows per gauge
  • Expose a small HTTP API (GET /readings?gauge=ID&from=ISO)
  • Alert when two neighboring gauges disagree by more than 15 cm for ten minutes in a row, which usually means a stuck float rather than a real surge
Heads up: gauge T-07 reports in feet. Conversion happens at ingest, not at query time.

Design

Each worker runs a loop like this:

for reading in queue.drain():
    row = convert(reading)      # feet -> meters happens here
    if row.valid:
        store.insert(row)
    else:
        log.warn("bad reading", reading.id)

See the runbook for deployment, or the missing page to check how 404s look.
